To draw the isometric projection of a square prism (base side $35\text{ mm}$, height $65\text{ mm}$) with its axis horizontal, follow these steps:

1. **Understand Orientation:** Since the axis is horizontal, the square ends will be perpendicular to the horizontal plane (appearing as vertical squares in the isometric view) and the long rectangular faces ($65\text{ mm} \times 35\text{ mm}$) will extend horizontally along the isometric axes.
2. **Use Isometric Scale:** Remember that isometric projection requires true lengths to be multiplied by $\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}}$ (or approximately $0.816$), whereas an isometric *drawing* uses true dimensions. Assuming an isometric projection is explicitly requested, scale down all dimensions by multiplying by $0.816$.
3. **Construction Steps:**
   - Draw baseline and establish a $30^\circ-30^\circ$ reference system.
   - Construct the scaled base square ($35\text{ mm} \times 0.816 = 28.56\text{ mm}$) vertically on the appropriate isometric plane.
   - Extrude the four corners along the horizontal isometric axis by the scaled length of the prism ($65\text{ mm} \times 0.816 = 53.04\text{ mm}$).
   - Complete the rear square face by connecting the extruded endpoints.
   - Darken visible outlines and use dashed lines for hidden edges if necessary.
proTip: Always distinguish clearly between an isometric scale (multiply true length by 0.816) and an isometric view/drawing (use true dimensions directly). Check the question wording carefully.
